intended_object: An auxiliary effective divisor n·(x)_∞ + (b−1)·(y)_∞ on the function field L/F_q(t). It is built so that every monomial x^i y^j with i ≤ n and j < b lies in its Riemann–Roch space, and it serves only the one-point Riemann-space lower-bound argument. I inferred this from the docstring, the module documentation and how the file uses it.
explanation: The body is just a linear combination of two pole divisors: n times the pole divisor of x plus (b−1) times the pole divisor of y. The module uses it as a "budget": it bounds the poles of the rectangular monomial grid, and its coefficient at a chosen place gives the arithmetic progression of pole levels used in the Riemann–Roch estimate. It is not a standard object from the literature. It is a convenience divisor built for one proof (the docstring says only that it "contains" the monomial grid, and its companion `planeCurveBidegreeGenusBudget` is likewise called a coarse budget). The formula does match what the docstring promises: x^i y^j has pole divisor at most i·(x)_∞ + j·(y)_∞ ≤ n·(x)_∞ + (b−1)·(y)_∞. When b = 0, natural-number subtraction gives b − 1 = 0, which does no harm because the grid is then empty. Since it is a proof device, it has no counterpart in Mathlib and no natural generality to judge it against.
